name: Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego
desc: Polish state-owned development bank managing government funds, guarantees and EU programmes for infrastructure, housing, municipalities and businesses.
markets: Serves Polish government bodies, municipalities and businesses; no known international customer base or expansion plans.
rationale: Public development bank with no consumer brand to market; sponsorship would be hard to justify, though domestic corporate visibility exists.

name: Bank Mandiri
desc: Indonesia's largest bank by assets, offering retail, corporate, SME and digital banking including the Livin' by Mandiri app.
markets: Core market Indonesia; overseas branches in Singapore, Hong Kong and Shanghai plus Timor-Leste; serves Indonesian corporates trading abroad.
rationale: Large consumer brand already active in Indonesian sport; F1 could support Singapore and Asia-wide corporate clients, though overseas reach is small.

name: Garanti BBVA
desc: One of Turkey's largest private banks, providing retail, SME, corporate and digital banking through several hundred branches.
markets: Mainly Turkey, with subsidiaries in Romania and the Netherlands; controlled by Spain's BBVA, which gives access to its international network.
rationale: Strong Turkish consumer brand; F1 hospitality could serve corporate clients, and the Turkish Grand Prix return would help, but footprint is mostly Turkey.

name: Halkbank
desc: Turkish state-controlled bank offering retail, commercial and SME banking, with a focus on small businesses and tradespeople.
markets: Customers mostly in Turkey; subsidiaries in North Macedonia, Serbia, Bahrain and Northern Cyprus; no known further expansion plans.
rationale: State-linked domestic lender with SME focus; limited brand-marketing culture, and legal and sanctions-related controversies make a global F1 deal unlikely.

name: Intrum
desc: Credit management company that collects debts and buys non-performing loans for banks, telecom, utility and retail clients across Europe.
markets: Operations across about 20 European countries, mainly the Nordics and continental Europe; clients are banks, utilities and retailers.
rationale: Business-to-business service with little consumer brand; hospitality could suit clients, but debt collection reputation and post-restructuring finances make F1 a poor fit.

name: National Bank of Greece
desc: Greece's oldest large bank, founded in 1841, providing retail, corporate and investment banking through a nationwide branch network.
markets: Customers mainly in Greece; small presence abroad, with no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Leading Greek bank with strong brand; F1 hospitality could reward corporate clients, but domestic focus and a regional-sponsorship culture limit global value.

name: National Bank of Kuwait
desc: Kuwait's first and largest bank, founded in 1952, providing retail, corporate, private and investment banking.
markets: Kuwait home market plus branches and subsidiaries across the Gulf, Egypt, London, Paris, Geneva, Singapore, New York and Shanghai.
rationale: Gulf bank with international footprint and wealthy clients; Bahrain and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix offer regional hospitality and private-banking networking.

name: Piraeus Bank
desc: One of Greece's four systemic banks, offering retail, corporate, investment and digital banking through hundreds of branches.
markets: Customers mainly in Greece; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Large Greek retail bank with national brand; F1 mostly out of scale for a domestic lender, though hospitality could serve corporate clients.

name: Alinma Bank
desc: Sharia-compliant Saudi bank founded in 2006, offering retail, corporate, SME and treasury banking.
markets: Customers in Saudi Arabia only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Saudi Grand Prix and Saudi national sport spending suit a visible local brand, but a domestic Islamic bank has limited global marketing need.

name: Bank of Maharashtra
desc: Indian state-owned public sector bank founded in 1935, providing retail, SME and corporate banking across India.
markets: Customers in India only; mainly the state of Maharashtra and other states; no overseas expansion plans known.
rationale: Domestic government-owned lender with little marketing culture; F1 offers little to its Indian retail and SME customers.

name: Banobras
desc: Mexican state development bank that finances public infrastructure and services such as roads, water, urban transport and municipal projects.
markets: Lends to Mexican federal, state and municipal governments and infrastructure projects; no international customer base.
rationale: Public development bank with no consumer brand; a Mexico Grand Prix tie is conceivable for infrastructure visibility but is unlikely.

name: Bridgit
desc: Australian privately owned non-bank lender based in Sydney, providing finance outside the traditional banking system.
markets: Based in Sydney; customers presumed Australian; no international activity confirmed.
rationale: Identity and scale unclear; small non-bank lender with no verified marketing budget, so F1 fit is weak.

name: Credit Agricole
desc: French cooperative banking group offering retail banking through regional banks and LCL, plus asset management, insurance and corporate banking.
markets: Retail in France, Italy, Poland and Egypt; corporate and investment banking plus Amundi asset management across Europe, the Americas and Asia.
rationale: Major global bank with strong French brand and corporate hospitality needs, though its sports sponsorship focus has been cycling and football.

name: DMI Finance
desc: Indian non-banking finance company providing digital consumer, personal and small business loans, often through partnerships with fintech and e-commerce platforms.
markets: Customers in India; lends through fintech, e-commerce and auto platform partners; no international plans known.
rationale: Digital lender with limited consumer brand marketing; F1 offers little value for Indian credit customers.

name: Dukhan Bank
desc: Qatari Islamic bank offering retail, corporate and investment banking, formed by merging Barwa Bank and International Bank of Qatar.
markets: Customers in Qatar; no verified overseas operations beyond limited international business.
rationale: Qatar hosts a Formula 1 Grand Prix and the bank has a visible local brand, but its footprint is largely domestic.
changed: Renamed Dukhan Bank in 2020 after Barwa and IBQ merger

name: Elevate Credit
desc: Online lender providing higher-cost instalment loans and credit lines to non-prime US consumers through brands such as Rise and Elastic.
markets: Customers in the United States; UK business was wound down; no known expansion plans.
rationale: Subprime consumer lender with reputational limits on high-profile sponsorship, and limited international reach.
changed: Taken private by Park Cities Asset Management in 2023

name: FirstCash
desc: Operator of more than 3,000 pawn stores in the United States and Latin America, plus a lease-to-own finance business.
markets: Stores across the US, Mexico, Guatemala, Colombia and El Salvador; also an American First Finance lease-to-own business.
rationale: Large Mexico footprint and Americas races could support brand awareness, though pawn lending is a niche with sensitive reputation.

name: Grupo Financiero Banorte
desc: Mexican financial group offering retail, corporate, insurance and pension services, and the country's largest Mexican-owned bank.
markets: Customers mainly in Mexico; some US-Mexico remittance and international corporate business.
rationale: Mexico City Grand Prix offers a strong home-market platform for a large consumer bank looking for national visibility.

name: Huatai Securities
desc: Chinese brokerage and investment bank providing retail brokerage, investment banking, asset management and wealth services.
markets: Customers mainly in mainland China, with a Hong Kong subsidiary; no verified further international expansion.
rationale: Large Chinese broker with Chinese Grand Prix exposure, but little consumer-style marketing and mostly domestic clients.

name: iCapital
desc: Fintech platform letting wealth managers, banks and asset managers access and distribute alternative investments such as private equity.
markets: Clients in the US, Europe and Asia including wealth managers, banks and fund managers; offices in London, Zurich and Hong Kong.
rationale: B2B fintech serving wealthy-client advisers; F1 hospitality fits relationship-building with banks and wealth managers worldwide.

name: Indian Bank
desc: Public sector bank founded in 1907 providing retail, MSME and corporate banking across India, enlarged by merging Allahabad Bank.
markets: Customers mainly in India; a few overseas branches in Singapore and Colombo; no expansion plans known.
rationale: Government-owned domestic lender; Indian Grand Prix absence and mass-market customers limit the value of an F1 tie.

name: Julius Baer Group
desc: Swiss private banking group managing client assets for wealthy individuals worldwide through wealth management and advisory services.
markets: Offices across Switzerland, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and the Americas serving high-net-worth clients worldwide.
rationale: Wealthy-client audience matches F1 hospitality; Julius Baer has used sport and events for client networking, making it a plausible premium partner.

name: OTP Bank
desc: Hungary's largest independent banking group, providing retail, SME and corporate banking in Hungary and several other markets.
markets: Operations in Hungary, Bulgaria, Croatia, Serbia, Slovenia, Albania, Ukraine, Moldova, Montenegro and Uzbekistan.
rationale: Hungarian Grand Prix is a home race, and multi-country footprint supports regional branding; marketing budgets may be modest.

name: Plaid
desc: Financial technology company whose software connects consumers' bank accounts to apps and supplies data and payment services to developers.
markets: Operates in the US, Canada, UK and several European countries; customers are app developers and financial firms.
rationale: Fintech infrastructure with developer focus; F1 could showcase brand to fintech partners, but consumer awareness is secondary.

name: Plata
desc: Mexican fintech offering a credit card and banking services to consumers in Mexico.
markets: Customers in Mexico; backed by large international investors; no overseas expansion confirmed.
rationale: Fast-growing consumer brand in Mexico where the Mexico City Grand Prix gives mass visibility; early stage limits budget certainty.

name: PRA Group
desc: Buyer of defaulted consumer debt portfolios from banks and lenders, collecting in the United States, Europe, Brazil and Australia.
markets: Operations in the US, Europe, Brazil and Australia; sells nothing to consumers, buying debt from lenders.
rationale: Debt collector with no consumer brand and sensitive public image; F1 offers little commercial benefit.

name: RBL Bank
desc: Indian private sector bank, formerly Ratnakar Bank, offering retail, credit card, SME and corporate banking through hundreds of branches.
markets: Customers in India only; large credit card business; no overseas expansion plans known.
rationale: Credit-card-led Indian lender with a consumer brand, but domestic focus and no Indian Grand Prix limit F1 value.
changed: Emirates NBD agreed in 2025 to acquire a majority stake

name: Scotiabank
desc: Canada's third-largest bank, offering retail, commercial, wealth and corporate banking with major businesses in Canada, Mexico, Chile, Peru and Colombia.
markets: Canada plus Mexico, Chile, Peru, Colombia and the Caribbean; corporate and investment banking in the US, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Canadian and Mexican Grands Prix match its two largest markets, and its global clients suit F1 hospitality.

name: Starling Bank
desc: UK digital bank founded in 2014 offering personal, joint and business accounts through an app, plus lending and banking-as-a-service.
markets: UK retail and business customers; its Engine software platform is licensed to banks abroad, but main operations are in the UK.
rationale: British brand-led challenger bank; the British Grand Prix and young affluent audience fit, though marketing budget is modest.

name: Talanx
desc: German insurance group, parent of HDI and Hannover Re, offering industrial, retail and reinsurance cover in many countries.
markets: Insurance and reinsurance in over 175 countries via HDI and Hannover Re, with major business in Europe, Americas and Asia.
rationale: B2B insurer and reinsurer with global clients; F1 hospitality could suit corporate relationships, though brand marketing is limited.

name: The Baldwin Group
desc: Insurance distribution firm selling commercial, personal and employee benefit insurance through independent agencies and its own advisers.
markets: Customers in the United States only; grows by acquiring independent agencies; no known international plans.
rationale: US insurance broker with limited consumer awareness; Miami and Austin races could support client hospitality, but the fit is not obvious.
changed: Renamed from BRP Group to The Baldwin Group in 2025

name: The Saudi Investment Bank
desc: Saudi bank offering corporate, retail, treasury and Islamic banking through branches across the kingdom.
markets: Customers in Saudi Arabia only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Saudi Grand Prix offers visibility for a mid-sized local bank, but its corporate focus and domestic scope limit global value.

name: Zurcher Kantonalbank
desc: Swiss cantonal bank owned by the Canton of Zurich, providing retail, corporate and private banking as one of Switzerland's largest.
markets: Customers mainly in the Zurich region and Switzerland; no known international expansion plans.
rationale: State-guaranteed regional bank with Swiss private-client base; F1 hospitality could suit wealthy clients, but cantonal mandate limits international marketing.

name: EXL
desc: Data analytics and digital operations company providing business process outsourcing, analytics and AI services to insurers, banks and healthcare clients.
markets: Clients mainly in the US and UK; delivery centres in India, the Philippines, the US and Europe.
rationale: B2B services firm with enterprise clients in insurance and banking; F1 offers hospitality and an AI and data showcase.

name: Bank Aljazira
desc: Saudi bank offering Sharia-compliant personal, corporate, treasury and investment banking through a branch network across Saudi Arabia.
markets: Customers in Saudi Arabia only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Saudi Grand Prix in Jeddah is its home city, so it could use the race for visibility, though budget and scope are domestic.

name: Credem Banca
desc: Italian bank known for private clients and small businesses, offering retail, corporate and wealth banking from its base in Emilia-Romagna.
markets: Customers in Italy only; Emilia-Romagna home base with branches across the country; no international expansion plans known.
rationale: Italian bank in motorsport heartland; Imola and Monza events could entertain business clients, though it is domestic and understated in marketing.

name: Cross River Bank
desc: Chartered US bank providing infrastructure for fintech firms, offering lending, payments and card issuing for partners such as Affirm.
markets: Serves US fintech and technology partners; consumers reached only through partners; no verified international operations.
rationale: B2B bank-as-infrastructure with limited consumer branding; F1 could help in fintech and crypto circles but domestic scope limits value.

name: Mashreq Bank
desc: Dubai-headquartered bank founded in 1967, one of the UAE's largest private banks, providing retail, corporate and investment banking.
markets: UAE home market plus operations in Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Egypt, London, New York, Hong Kong and India.
rationale: Abu Dhabi Grand Prix is on home soil and its multi-region corporate clients suit hospitality; a strong Gulf marketing brand.

name: Tata Capital
desc: Non-banking financial company in the Tata Group offering consumer, commercial and infrastructure loans, wealth management and cards.
markets: Customers in India only; offers loans, wealth and cards through branches and digital channels; no overseas expansion known.
rationale: Tata brand with large Indian reach; group sibling Tata Communications already backs F1, but Tata Capital itself is a domestic lender.
f1: Group link: Tata Communications (Tata group) is a Formula 1 partner.

name: Union Bank of India
desc: Indian public sector bank formed in 1919, enlarged by 2020 mergers with Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank, offering retail banking.
markets: Customers mainly in India; small overseas network of branches and a UK subsidiary; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Government-owned domestic lender with mass-market customers across India; F1 offers limited commercial return and little brand relevance.
changed: Merged with Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank in 2020

name: Westpac
desc: One of Australia's four major banks, founded in 1817, providing retail, business and institutional banking in Australia and New Zealand.
markets: Customers in Australia and New Zealand, with institutional banking offices in Asia, the US and the UK.
rationale: Major Australian consumer bank with long sports sponsorship culture; the Australian Grand Prix gives home-market visibility.

name: MNT-Halan
desc: Egyptian fintech group offering consumer finance, small business loans, payments and mobility services through the Halan and MNT businesses.
markets: Customers in Egypt only; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Fast-growing Egyptian consumer brand with young users; F1 offers visibility, but its audience and budget are largely domestic.

name: Financeit
desc: Point-of-sale financing platform providing consumer loans for home improvement and other big-ticket purchases through contractors and retailers.
markets: Operates in Canada, lending through contractors and retailers; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: B2B2C lender whose partners are small contractors; Canadian Grand Prix could entertain partners, but the brand has little international need.

name: Kaspi.kz
desc: Kazakhstan fintech super-app and bank offering payments, marketplace shopping and consumer finance to millions of customers.
markets: Core market Kazakhstan; expanded into Turkey through its 2024 purchase of Hepsiburada, the Turkish e-commerce platform.
rationale: Dominant consumer brand with ambitions beyond Kazakhstan; F1 could support its Turkey expansion and brand building.

name: Mission Lane
desc: US credit card issuer for consumers who are building or rebuilding credit.
markets: Customers in the United States only; no international operations known.
rationale: Subprime-focused card issuer with limited marketing scale; F1 would be an unusually costly platform for its audience.

name: PowerPay
desc: Digital lending platform offering low-rate consumer financing, probably for home improvement and similar purchases.
markets: Based in Pennsylvania; customers presumed to be in the United States; no international activity confirmed.
rationale: Little is known about its scale or marketing; F1 fit appears weak.

name: Solfacil
desc: Brazilian fintech providing financing and a marketplace for solar energy installers and their customers.
markets: Customers are solar installers and homeowners in Brazil; no verified international operations.
rationale: Brazilian Grand Prix in Sao Paulo is its home race; a sustainability message fits, but scale and consumer reach are limited.

name: InCred
desc: Indian non-banking finance company offering personal loans, education loans and wealth management services.
markets: Customers in India only; no international operations or expansion plans known.
rationale: Domestic lender and wealth group with limited consumer brand marketing; F1 has little relevance for its customers.

name: Zolve
desc: Neobank for immigrants, helping newcomers to the US get credit cards and bank accounts using their foreign credit history.
markets: Customers are immigrants arriving in the United States; no verified expansion beyond the US.
rationale: Niche fintech targeting immigrants; F1 could reach internationally mobile audiences, but its marketing budget is small.

name: Al Ahli Bank of Kuwait
desc: Kuwaiti commercial bank providing retail, corporate and private banking, including Islamic-style financial services, to customers in Kuwait.
markets: Customers mainly in Kuwait; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Established Kuwaiti bank; Gulf Grands Prix provide regional visibility, but its focus is domestic with modest marketing scale.

name: BADEA
desc: Intergovernmental Arab development finance institution providing loans and grants for economic development projects in African countries.
markets: Finances development projects in Africa, funded by Arab member states; no commercial customers.
rationale: Intergovernmental development lender with no consumer or commercial brand; sponsorship is highly unlikely.

name: Banca Transilvania
desc: Romania's largest bank by assets, providing retail, SME and corporate banking, headquartered in Cluj-Napoca.
markets: Customers mainly in Romania; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Dominant Romanian consumer bank; no Romanian race, so F1 value is mainly brand prestige and corporate hospitality.

name: Banco do Brasil
desc: Brazil's largest bank by assets, majority state-owned, providing retail, corporate, agribusiness and investment banking through thousands of branches.
markets: Core market Brazil, with branches and subsidiaries in the US, Europe, Asia and Latin America serving Brazilian companies.
rationale: Large Brazilian consumer brand with long sports sponsorship history; Sao Paulo Grand Prix is a home race.

name: Bladex
desc: Multinational bank founded in 1978 providing trade finance and financial services to banks and companies across Latin America.
markets: Serves financial institutions and corporates across Latin America, with offices in several countries and New York.
rationale: Business-to-business trade bank; hospitality at Latin American races could suit clients, but mass-market marketing is irrelevant.

name: CAF - Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean
desc: Multilateral development bank financing infrastructure, sustainability and social projects in Latin America and the Caribbean for its member governments.
markets: Lends to member governments and companies in Latin America and the Caribbean; formerly named Corporacion Andina de Fomento.
rationale: Multilateral institution with no consumer brand; sponsorship of a commercial sport is highly unlikely.

name: Monzo
desc: London-based digital bank founded in 2015 providing current accounts, savings, loans and business accounts through its coral-pink card and app.
markets: Customers mostly in the UK; has pursued expansion into the US and Ireland.
rationale: Strong British consumer brand with young customers; British Grand Prix and global digital audience suit its growth ambitions.

name: Mr. Cooper Group
desc: Mortgage servicer and originator servicing about a million loans for homeowners and lenders across the United States.
markets: Customers in the United States only; no international operations.
rationale: Domestic mortgage servicer with limited consumer choice or brand loyalty; F1 audience offers little commercial benefit.

name: Opportunity Finance Network
desc: US non-profit network of community development financial institutions that lend to underserved communities and small businesses.
markets: Members are US community lenders serving underserved areas; no international operations.
rationale: Non-profit association with a social mission; commercial sponsorship of F1 is highly unlikely.

name: Export-Import Bank of Korea
desc: South Korean state-owned policy bank providing export and import financing, overseas investment loans and development cooperation funds.
markets: Finances Korean exporters and overseas projects, with offices across Asia, Europe, the Americas and the Middle East.
rationale: Policy bank with no consumer brand; sponsorship is unlikely, though supporting Korean exporters could justify a niche tie.

name: Ziraat Bank
desc: Turkey's largest state-owned bank, providing retail, agricultural, commercial and corporate banking through a large branch network.
markets: Core market Turkey, with subsidiaries and branches in Germany, Bosnia, Central Asia and the Middle East.
rationale: Large Turkish consumer brand; Turkey's possible Grand Prix return and Turkish diaspora in Europe provide marketing logic.

name: Apollo PK AirFinance
desc: Provider of loans secured by aircraft, serving airlines and aircraft lessors.
markets: Location per Crunchbase is in Bavaria; customers are airlines and lessors, but countries served are not confirmed.
rationale: Niche aircraft financier with a B2B client base; limited consumer brand, so F1 relevance is weak.

name: Arab National Bank
desc: Saudi bank providing retail, corporate, treasury, private banking and Islamic banking services across the kingdom.
markets: Customers in Saudi Arabia; no verified international operations.
rationale: Saudi Grand Prix offers visibility for a mid-sized Saudi bank, but domestic scope limits wider marketing value.

name: Bank of Nanjing
desc: Chinese city commercial bank providing retail, corporate and treasury banking, headquartered in Nanjing, Jiangsu.
markets: Customers in China, mainly Jiangsu province and the Yangtze River Delta; no international operations known.
rationale: Regional Chinese bank with little global marketing need; Chinese Grand Prix is distant from its customers.

name: Berlin Hyp
desc: German commercial real estate bank providing property financing, notably for office, retail, logistics and residential projects.
markets: Finances commercial property in Germany and other European markets; owned by LBBW.
rationale: Property lender with institutional clients and little consumer brand; F1 hospitality could suit investors, but fit is modest.

name: Gulf International Bank
desc: Bahrain-based wholesale bank offering corporate, investment, treasury and asset management services, owned by the six Gulf Cooperation Council states.
markets: Operations in Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, London, New York and Switzerland serving Gulf governments and corporates.
rationale: Bahrain hosts a Grand Prix and the bank serves Gulf corporates, but it is wholesale-focused with little consumer branding.

name: Northern Trust
desc: Financial institution founded in 1889 providing asset servicing, wealth management and asset management for institutions and wealthy families.
markets: Offices across North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific serving institutional investors and high-net-worth clients.
rationale: Wealth and institutional clients match F1 hospitality; Northern Trust has used major sports sponsorship, though F1 is unproven for it.

name: PNB Housing Finance
desc: Indian housing finance company providing home loans, loans against property and construction finance.
markets: Customers in India only; no international operations or plans known.
rationale: Domestic mortgage lender with no international need; F1 has weak relevance despite its Punjab National Bank heritage.

name: Qatar International Islamic Bank
desc: Doha-based Sharia-compliant bank offering retail, corporate and investment banking in Qatar.
markets: Customers mainly in Qatar; no verified international operations.
rationale: Qatar hosts a Grand Prix and the bank may value local visibility, but its domestic scope limits value.

name: Raymond James
desc: Financial services firm offering wealth management, investment banking, asset management and brokerage services to individuals and institutions.
markets: Advisers and clients mainly in the US and Canada, with investment banking operations in the UK and Europe.
rationale: Wealthy-client base suits hospitality; Miami and Austin Grands Prix could support advisers, but international need is limited.

name: ZhongAn Online P&C Insurance
desc: China's first fully online property and casualty insurer, founded in 2013, selling digital insurance through partner platforms.
markets: Customers mainly in China; also runs the ZA Bank digital bank in Hong Kong and technology exports in Asia.
rationale: Digital insurer with large platform audience in China; F1 could support technology and Hong Kong brand building, but is mostly domestic.

name: Zopa
desc: London-based UK digital bank founded in 2005 as a peer-to-peer lender, which received a banking licence in 2020.
markets: Customers in the UK only; offers savings, loans and credit cards; no confirmed international plans.
rationale: British consumer fintech with growing brand awareness; British Grand Prix gives home visibility, though budget is limited.

name: ABN AMRO Bank
desc: Dutch bank providing retail, private and corporate banking, with a strong position in the Netherlands and selected international businesses.
markets: Core market Netherlands, with operations in Germany, France, Belgium and corporate banking in the US and Asia.
rationale: Dutch home Grand Prix at Zandvoort and corporate clients with global trade suit F1 hospitality; Dutch state is a major shareholder.

name: Bank of Bahrain and Kuwait
desc: Bahrain financial group founded in 1971, offering retail, corporate and Islamic banking in Bahrain and nearby markets.
markets: Operations in Bahrain and Kuwait, with branches and associates elsewhere in the Gulf and India.
rationale: Bahrain hosts a Grand Prix and the bank has strong local brand, giving natural home-race hospitality value.

name: Federal Bank
desc: Indian private sector bank founded in 1931 and based in Aluva, Kerala, offering retail, NRI, SME and corporate banking.
markets: Customers mainly in India, with strong non-resident Indian business from Kerala; no overseas expansion known.
rationale: Kerala consumer bank with a diaspora customer base; F1 would be a stretch for its marketing scale.

name: India Exim Bank
desc: Indian government-owned financial institution created in 1982 to finance and promote international trade and project exports.
markets: Lines of credit and offices across Africa, Asia and other regions to support Indian exporters and overseas projects.
rationale: Government export bank with no consumer brand; sponsorship of F1 is highly unlikely.

name: LIQUiDITY Group
desc: New York financial services firm that deploys capital using advanced technology to speed up credit.
markets: Based in New York; customers presumed American; no international operations confirmed.
rationale: Little is known about its scale or customers; no evident marketing case for F1.

name: Shenzhen Rural Commercial Bank
desc: Chinese commercial bank headquartered in Shenzhen, Guangdong, serving retail, SME and corporate customers.
markets: Customers in Shenzhen and Guangdong; no international operations known.
rationale: Local Chinese bank with limited marketing need beyond its home region; F1 fit is weak.

name: Younited
desc: Paris-based European consumer credit and open banking fintech, founded in 2009, offering instalment loans and payments in several countries.
markets: Operates in France, Italy, Spain, Portugal and Germany through direct lending and partner distribution.
rationale: Pan-European fintech seeking brand growth; F1 could lift consumer awareness, though its budget is moderate.

name: Barq
desc: Saudi fintech offering a financial app, debit card and social platform.
markets: Based in Riyadh; customers presumed in Saudi Arabia; no international operations confirmed.
rationale: Young Saudi fintech brand; Saudi Grand Prix could raise awareness, but marketing budget is uncertain.

name: Rizz Lending
desc: Utah lender specialising in loans for exotic and collector cars, according to Crunchbase.
markets: Based in Utah; customers are US car collectors; no international operations known.
rationale: Niche lender serving luxury car owners, so audience overlaps with F1 fans, but its size is likely very small.

name: Columbia Banking System
desc: Bank holding company operating Columbia Bank and Umpqua branches, providing commercial and consumer banking across the western United States.
markets: Customers in the western United States; no international operations.
rationale: Regional US bank with local brand; Las Vegas and Austin races are nearby, but a global platform adds little.
changed: Merged with Umpqua in 2023; acquired Pacific Premier in 2025

name: Alpha Bank
desc: Major Greek bank offering retail, SME and corporate banking through branches across Greece.
markets: Customers mainly in Greece, with a smaller presence in Cyprus; no major new expansion known.
rationale: Large Greek retail bank; F1 offers prestige and corporate hospitality, but customers and marketing are domestic.

name: Israel Discount Bank
desc: One of Israel's largest banks, providing retail, commercial and private banking in Israel and the United States.
markets: Core market Israel, with a US subsidiary in New York and branches serving American customers.
rationale: Large Israeli bank with US operations; F1 hospitality could serve corporate clients, but marketing focus is domestic.

name: mBank
desc: Polish retail and corporate bank launched in 2000 as Poland's first online bank, majority-owned by Commerzbank.
markets: Customers in Poland, with operations in the Czech Republic and Slovakia; owned by Germany's Commerzbank.
rationale: Digital-first Polish brand with young customers; F1 could support regional brand building, though marketing spend is local.

name: Sohar International
desc: Omani bank formed from the 2020 merger of Sohar Bank and HSBC Oman, offering retail, corporate and Islamic banking.
markets: Customers in Oman only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Omani bank with local brand; no Omani race, and F1 would be a stretch for its scale.

name: Standard Bank Group
desc: Africa's largest bank by assets, providing retail, business and corporate banking across Africa and selected international markets.
markets: Operations in South Africa and about 20 African countries, plus offices in London, New York, Dubai and China.
rationale: Pan-African brand with corporate hospitality needs; no African race currently, though F1 has interest in a return.

name: Kuwait International Bank
desc: Kuwaiti Islamic bank providing Sharia-compliant retail, corporate and investment banking services.
markets: Customers in Kuwait only; no verified international operations.
rationale: Local Islamic bank with modest marketing scale; Gulf Grands Prix provide some regional visibility.

name: Maybank
desc: Malaysia's largest bank, providing retail, commercial, investment banking and Islamic banking across Southeast Asia.
markets: Operations in Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia plus Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia, Hong Kong and London.
rationale: Large Asian bank with major sports sponsorship history; Singapore and Malaysian audiences make F1 a plausible regional brand platform.

name: Ajman Bank
desc: Islamic commercial bank in the emirate of Ajman, UAE, providing retail, business and treasury services under Sharia principles.
markets: Customers in the UAE only; no verified international operations.
rationale: UAE hosts the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, but Ajman Bank is small and locally focused.

name: Alkami Technology
desc: Cloud-based digital banking platform company providing online and mobile banking software to US banks and credit unions.
markets: Customers are US banks and credit unions; no international operations.
rationale: B2B software vendor to American banks; F1 could support client hospitality, but audience is narrow and domestic.

name: D360 Bank
desc: Saudi digital bank offering mobile-based banking services to individuals and businesses.
markets: Customers in Saudi Arabia; digital-only model; no verified international operations.
rationale: New Saudi digital bank seeking young customers; Saudi Grand Prix offers brand visibility, though its marketing budget is unproven.

name: Deutsche Boerse Group
desc: Operator of the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Eurex derivatives exchange, Xetra and Clearstream, providing trading, clearing, settlement and data services.
markets: Exchanges, clearing and custody serving financial institutions across Europe, the Americas and Asia, with offices in London, New York and Singapore.
rationale: B2B market infrastructure with institutional clients; F1 hospitality could serve banks and traders, though brand marketing is limited.

name: Helvetia Baloise Holding
desc: Swiss insurer formed by the 2025 merger of Helvetia and Baloise, offering life, non-life and pension insurance in Europe.
markets: Insurance in Switzerland, Germany, Italy, Spain, Austria, France and Benelux; no non-European expansion known.
rationale: Large Swiss insurer with strong brand across Europe; Swiss and European audiences suit hospitality, though sports sponsorship has focused elsewhere.

name: Jana Small Finance Bank
desc: Indian small finance bank that grew from the microfinance lender Janalakshmi Financial Services, providing loans and deposits to underserved customers.
markets: Customers in India only, mainly lower-income and small business borrowers; no international operations.
rationale: Inclusion-focused domestic lender with little consumer marketing; F1 has little relevance to its borrowers.
changed: Converted to a small finance bank in 2018

name: KA Fund Advisors
